themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% increase, z-score 7.49), suggesting either systematic removal, theft, or rapid infrastructure degradation in Elmhurst/South Corona.
evidence: 4 missing street sign complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.49)
967% spike from 8-week average represents statistically significant deviation
Pattern emerged suddenly this week with no prior escalation signal
reporting_angles: Ground reconnaissance: walk affected neighborhoods to identify missing signs and photograph gaps; interview residents about safety/navigation impacts
NYPD/DOT coordination: investigate whether signs are being stolen for scrap or removed due to construction/maintenance; cross-reference with DOB permit activity (282 filings in last 90 days)

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge Across District
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise jumped to 43 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.4 weekly average (222% increase, z-score 5.65), while park noise hit 5 complaints this week vs. 1.0 average (400% increase, z-score 4.0), suggesting either new event activity, construction, or quality-of-life deterioration across multiple venues.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 43 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.4 weekly average (222% spike, z-score 5.65)
Park noise: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% spike, z-score 4.0)
Commercial noise also elevated 2 weeks ago (22 complaints vs. 7.4 avg), suggesting sustained pressure
Residential noise remains highest category at 1,468 over 90 days, indicating chronic baseline
reporting_angles: Identify what changed this week: new venue openings, construction projects, event permits, or nightlife expansion; check NYPD incident data and 311 complaint location clusters
Interview affected residents in high-complaint census tracts; determine if noise is sources are consistent (bars, construction, traffic) or diffuse

themes_detail.label: Public Urination Emergent Issue
themes_detail.summary: Public urination complaints hit 3 reports THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35), a rare but sharp signal that may indicate either homeless encampment growth, lack of public restrooms, or substance use clustering.
evidence: 3 urinating in public complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Community Board repeatedly requests DHS funding for homeless services (2 separate budget line items), indicating known chronic homelessness
Heat/hot water complaints at 2,061 over 90 days suggest housing stress that may correlate with street population
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaint locations to identify geographic hotspot; determine if concentrated in parks (where 400% park noise spike occurred) or commercial areas
Interview DHS, outreach teams, and local organizations about recent changes in unsheltered population size or encampment locations; cross-reference with police quality-of-life enforcement data

themes_detail.label: Elevator Safety Crisis in High-Rises
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked to 30 last week vs. 7.5 weekly average (300% increase, z-score 6.63), affecting residents in multifamily buildings and raising concerns about maintenance, aging infrastructure, or inspectional enforcement gaps.
evidence: 30 elevator complaints last week vs. 7.5 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 6.63)
282 DOB alteration permits filed in last 90 days (202 alteration filings); unclear if elevator work included or if backlog exists
Two active ULURP rezonings at 50-20 and 47-03 108th Street may signal building conversions or significant residential development affecting elevator demand
reporting_angles: FOIL DOB elevator inspection records for CD 404 in last 90 days; identify buildings with repeat violations or deferred repairs
Interview landlords, residents of affected buildings, and DOB about inspection backlogs; determine if spike is one building or district-wide pattern
Safety angle: elderly, mobility-impaired residents in buildings without functioning elevators; accessibility implications for schools and senior centers

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Team Surge
themes_detail.summary: SPIT complaints exploded to 5 two weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% increase, z-score 10.97, highest z-score on board), likely indicating concentrated DOE or HPD enforcement activity; warrants investigation into what triggered deployment and what violations were targeted.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1900% spike, z-score 10.97—highest on entire spike list)
SPIT is typically DOE or HPD enforcement unit, suggesting targeted inspection campaign
Community Board budget history includes repeated requests for DOE capital investment and family services, suggesting known educational/facility gaps
reporting_angles: Contact DOE and HPD press offices to learn what triggered SPIT deployment 2 weeks ago; was it response to 311 complaints, tip line, or proactive enforcement?
Determine which schools, apartments, or facilities were inspected and for what violations; public records may reveal pattern
